question_text: In PCB design, what is "crosstalk," and what are the two physical mechanisms that cause it between adjacent traces?
answer_text: Crosstalk is unwanted noise transferred from an "aggressor" trace to a "victim" trace. It is caused by Capacitive coupling and Inductive coupling.
explanation_text: Capacitive coupling happens when the voltage rapidly changes on the aggressor (dV/dt), pushing current into the victim via parasitic fringe capacitance between the traces. Inductive coupling happens when the current rapidly changes on the aggressor (dI/dt), creating a magnetic field that induces a voltage in the victim via mutual inductance.
bonus_question_text: Is crosstalk worse when the traces run parallel for a long distance?
bonus_answer_text: Yes. The longer the traces run parallel, the larger the mutual capacitance and inductance become, leading to much stronger coupling.
